fieldMarks: Smallest carnivore in the family: long tubular body, short tail under a quarter of head-body length
Winter coat pure white in northern animals, but never a black tail tip
Summer: rusty chocolate-brown back, white belly
North American animals average about 45 g and about 190 mm including tail
behavior: Active day or night through the year
Specialist on small mammals, especially voles, lemmings and mice; also other small vertebrates, insects or worms when rodents are scarce
Uses abandoned burrows of prey; hunts in subnivean tunnels
habitat: Open forests, farmland, grassy fields and meadows, riparian woodland, hedgerows, alpine meadows, scrub, prairies and coastal dunes; generally avoids deep dense forest.
range: Circumboreal. Most of Canada and Alaska, south to British Columbia, Montana, Wyoming, Oklahoma, Missouri, Ohio, Virginia and along the Appalachians; range has expanded south in the Great Plains since the mid-1960s.
